PLAY · BEGINNING SOUNDS

Sound Detective

Look at the letter in the bubble, say its sound, then circle every picture that starts with it.

HOW TO DO IT

Read, then draw.

Look at the letter in the bubble, say its sound, then circle every picture that starts with it.

That one starts with the sound!

YOUR PENCIL CASE

Pick your tools.

Pencil, nine crayons, an eraser, undo, redo and clear appear right here and work straight on the picture. Save keeps your finished work as a picture.

MY PROGRESS

Save it to keep it.

This adventure is cleared for you the moment you save your finished picture. Nothing counts until then — opening the page is just opening the door.

Cleared! Case closed! Your saved work is in your downloads, and the ribbon is on in the library.

      FOR GROWN-UPS

      Why this adventure helps.

      This activity trains beginning sounds right on the adventure picture, with one short written instruction a grown-up can read aloud. Nothing is graded and nothing is scored — the win is a child who picked up a pencil, played with the sounds they hear in words, and saved work they are proud of. Saying the sounds cleanly (sss, not “suh”) as they draw is exactly how reading research says to teach them.

      Prefer paper? The Sound Detective worksheet brings the same activity to the kitchen table with a parent-read sound script and an answer line — printing a worksheet never marks a class complete.
